statements.impact_statement: Not exposed: new sink introduced by PR #51's first-login walkthrough. At tour-controller.ts:52, `res.send(await TourService.save(req.user!.id, req.body))` sends the return value of TourService.save (tour-service.ts:58-65), which is `{ status: TourStatus, step: number, tutorialCourseId: string | null }`. Nothing from `req.body` reaches the response as a string: TourService.parse (tour-service.ts:68-85) strict-validates `status` against the TourStatus Prisma enum (`STATUSES.includes(status)`) and coerces `step` through `boundedInteger(..., { min: 0, max: TOUR_STEP_COUNT - 1 })`, so the returned `status` is one of a fixed enum set and `step` is an integer; `tutorialCourseId` is a server-computed DB id from DefaultTutorialService.id(). Express `res.send` on an object auto-serialises to JSON with Content-Type application/json, which browsers cannot render as HTML. Same pattern and disposition as the sibling sinks in curriculum-controller.ts.

Not exposed: REEVALUATE (touched) — curriculum-controller.ts was edited by PR #51 (course-access additions upstream in the file), so the standing not_affected needs re-verification. Re-verified: the sink at line 539 is unchanged in shape — `res.send(result)` where `result` is either EditLeaseService.release (edit-lease-service.ts:84-86, returns `{ released: boolean }` from `count > 0`) or EditLeaseService.releaseAll (edit-lease-service.ts:90-92, returns `{ released: number }` from a Prisma `updateMany` count). Neither payload interpolates any user-supplied string — the shape is a single literal key and a server-computed primitive. Express `res.send` on an object serialises to JSON with Content-Type application/json, which browsers cannot render as HTML. The nosemgrep marker on line 538 is intact. Original disposition re-confirmed with a fresh 90-day window.
